basis: Renal cystic disease defines ADPKD. Hepatic cysts occur in 80-99% but usually preserve function; damaging liver involvement is a minority. Hypertension is separately diagnosed.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic cysts occur in 80-99%, but clinically damaging liver involvement is below ~30%; cyst presence alone does not establish impaired function.

basis: Complement deficiency with lupus-like immune dysregulation; discoid lesions in 4/4 and inflammatory arthritis in 1/3 (~33%). An isolated oral ulcer does not establish lasting mucosal damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: oral ulcer reported in 1/1 assessed patient, without evidence of persistent damaging mucosal disease or a major diagnostic criterion.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: inflammatory arthritis in 1/3 (~33%) supports direct joint involvement as part of the immune dysregulation phenotype; arthralgia alone would not qualify.

basis: Inherited defects of hepatic bilirubin metabolism or transport define this umbrella. Neurologic injury occurs in severe subtypes rather than most patients.

decisions.hepatic: primary: defective hepatic bilirubin conjugation or transport defines most constituent disorders; primary localization does not require destructive liver injury.

basis: Developmental disability and seizures are central. Scoliosis varies by duplication; a frequency of at least 30% across this broad umbrella is not established. Hypotonia is neurologic.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis is described qualitatively as common, but damaging skeletal involvement in at least ~30% across the heterogeneous duplication group is not established.

basis: Combined immunodeficiency with defining severe malabsorption and protracted diarrhea in 30-79%. Separately diagnosed respiratory infections and infectious hepatobiliary disease are excluded.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: severe malabsorption is a defining intestinal loss of function, supported by protracted diarrhea in 30-79%; recurrent enteric infections alone would not qualify.

basis: Inherited renal tubular transport dysfunction; electrolyte, solute and acid-base disturbances characterize most major subgroups. Extrarenal organ damage is subtype-dependent.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: disordered electrolyte or acid-base handling characterizes most major tubular transport disorders and directly meets the metabolic axis definition.

basis: Retinal dystrophy, cataracts and intellectual disability define the syndrome. Dental malocclusion occurs in 3/3; brachydactyly in 30-79%. Short stature alone does not establish skeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: brachydactyly occurs in 30-79%, supporting congenital skeletal involvement; short stature alone does not establish a primary skeletal disorder.

basis: Postsynaptic neuromuscular junction dysfunction defines CMS3B. Ptosis, ophthalmoplegia and respiratory weakness reflect impaired transmission rather than intrinsic eye or lung disease.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis and ophthalmoplegia in 1/1 reflect neuromuscular junction dysfunction; they do not establish direct disease of ocular structures.

basis: Ichthyosis, congenital mouth/lip abnormalities and digital anomalies form the defining triad. Oral structural abnormalities support primary localization without requiring secondary dysfunction.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: congenital small mouth and lip malformations constitute the syndrome's defining oral component; the mouth is explicitly within the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Bile duct paucity and cardiovascular defects define Alagille syndrome; renal structural or functional abnormalities occur in ~39%. Butterfly vertebrae and embryotoxon usually preserve function.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: butterfly vertebrae occur in roughly 50% and are diagnostically useful, but usually cause no functional damage; their frequency alone does not satisfy the damage requirement.
